text:
carla: quick RFC follow-up — we still need a decision on redispatching stalled controlplane requests from a per-customer peering to a Privatelink fallback. main concerns: preserving client src ip for audit, TLS identity continuity, and not blowing up latency SLOs.
ben: +1 on making this decision today. we saw a replay last week where stuck peering caused 503s for a few mins.
dave: can we clarify 'redispatch' — do you mean we re-resolve and route via privatelink from the edge if peering path fails mid-conn?
carla: yes. idea: detect egress failure at relay, short-circuit to privatelink for that tenant's remaining requests. keep original client certs (mutual TLS) by doing TLS passthrough when possible.
erin: TLS passthrough preserves identity but blocks us from doing any header enrichment/observability. is that acceptable for Dedicated customers?
alice: for Dedicated / Private customers we promised audit logs. passthrough + L7 sampling means we lose per-request app-level fields. maybe we can do a minimal proxy that preserves src ip via X-Tenant-Source header and piggyback signed attestation?
frank: signed attestation sounds heavy. simpler: when we switch to privatelink, create an ephemeral tunnel that preserves src ip using proxy protocol v2 + keepalive. downside: nat rules in customer VPC may drop proxy-proto frames.
dave: many customers use TGW + firewall that strips unknown L4 proto. Not reliable.
erin: what about doing redispatch at TCP level only for long-lived streams, and for short HTTP calls do full TLS termination then re-initiate TLS to upstream with a short-lived mTLS cert that includes original subject as an aud claim? preserves audit, but we need KMS + rotation flow.
ben: that aud-claim approach seems reasonable and gives us observability. operational cost: we need auto-issuing certs scoped per-redispatch and rotation TTL ~1m. is that doable?
frank: yes, doable. vault + signer + audit entry. but we must be careful: if peering bounces frequently, we could be issuing lots of certs. add a debounce window (30s) per-tenant.
alice: also add a route-affinity hint so subsequent requests in same session prefer the new path for steady-state, but expire after the tenant's session TTL. avoids constant flip-flopping.
carla: good. latency SLO check: re-TLS adds ~12-40ms cold, plus signing latency ~10-20ms. our 99p SLO is 120ms on auth path — we can absorb if we keep it rare.
dave: fallback criteria? suggest: 1) detect consecutive TCP reset / connect timeout to peering >3 within 15s OR controlplane health endpoint failing L7 checks, 2) redispatch bounded to X requests or 30s.
erin: ops: we need a dashboard for redispatch events per-tenant + alert on rate ( >1/min ).
ops-bot: created issue INFRA-7432: add redispatch metric & per-tenant alert. ETA: 2w. :white_check_mark:
ben: security note: customer-approved contracts might forbid re-terminating TLS in some regulated accounts. fallback must be opt-in per-tenant.
carla: agreed. default behavior = try passthrough; if tenant opt-out, do not reterminate; instead keep retrying peering or surface error. document in onboarding.
frank: implementation sketch: 
```
edge relay detects peering failure -> check tenant config (opt-in reterminate?) -> attempt tcp-level passthrough
if passthrough blocked -> sign redispatch cert and reterminate -> route via privatelink
record audit: tenant, original-subject, new-cert-id, reason
```
alice: please also publish a short runbook for SRE: how to force a redispatch back to peering, how to revoke ephemeral certs if compromised.
carla: decision summary:
- allow redispatch to Privatelink as fallback (opt-in per-tenant)
- try TCP passthrough first; if blocked, reterminate TLS with ephemeral cert containing original subject aud claim
- debounce + affinity windows to avoid flapping (30s debounce, 5m affinity expiry)
- metric + alert (INFRA-7432) and onboarding opt-out flag
- implement signing via existing KMS/vault pipeline, TTL ~60s, rotate aggressively
Action items: ben -> update onboarding docs, erin -> add dashboard/alert, frank -> prototype cert signing + debounce logic, alice -> runbook.
ben: I'll PR onboarding text today.
frank: I'll spike the signer tomorrow and drop notes in the arch RFC thread.
carla: thanks all. feel free to @carla if you hit any corner cases. :thumbsup:
